Incident INC-REH-0001, hypothesis H6. Session nonce: biho-tasi-jaro-kobu-vopo-luko-suji-kinu-buvo-tuli-tizo

Hypothesis: H3: Make line posting idempotent so retries cannot double-book regardless of session lifetime
Root cause: Alternative theory of the defect's locus: the duplicate arises because `pending()`/`post_line` carry no record of what has already reached books:/lines, so correctness depends entirely on a fragile object-lifetime invariant inside the retried closure. Under that reading the session relocation was merely the trigger; the real root cause is a non-idempotent posting path that any retry (or caller passing a stale/absent session) can duplicate.
Approach: Give each pending line a stable idempotency key (e.g. batch id + line id/sequence) and make the booking path refuse to re-post an already-posted key: either have `PostingSession` track posted keys and exclude them from `pending()` after reconciling against `list_lines` for books:/lines on a fresh session, or have `post_line` short-circuit when the key is already present. Then a re-run of `book_pending_lines` after a RateLimited from `fx_rate` resumes rather than re-books, even if a fresh PostingSession is constructed. Do not weaken retry/backoff behavior, do not change tool names or the books:/lines contract beyond the added key, and do not touch the grader. If this lands alongside the H1 invariant it must still pass with the session hoisted, so keep the two mechanisms independent.

Intent constraints of the code you are changing (keep them; the quotes are the original
author's words):
- A rate limit must retry the pass as resumption, never as re-booking.: "+    """Book every pending line of ``batch`` in USD; a rate limit retries the whole pass.""""
- The double-booking path named by the author is the behavior that must become impossible.: "If the caller passes no session and a 429 hits mid-pass, the retry builds a fresh session and re-books lines the first attempt already posted. That is a double-booking risk, and the existing tests don't exercise it."
- Retry semantics themselves were never meant to change; only the retried pass's naming/documentation was in scope, so retry policy must stay intact.: "Refactor `reconcile`'s retry logic for readability: name the retried pass and document it."
- Bookings must survive a retry, which this idempotency guarantee must uphold rather than contradict.: "-    session = session or PostingSession(batch)  # outside the retried scope: survives retries"

content.text:
Retrying `reconcile` without a session no longer re-books lines the first attempt already posted. `python -m pytest -q` passes (4 passed). I couldn't run an ad-hoc script for the mid-pass 429 case, because writing the file was denied. So that exact scenario has no test coverage yet.

All edits are in `practice_ledger/reconcile.py`:
- **Skip booked lines:** `PostingSession.pending()` now leaves out any line whose key is already in the session's booked set. `done` is now `not pending()`.
- **Adopt what the books hold:** a new `PostingSession.sync_with_books()` reads `list_lines(batch.ref)` and adds those line keys to the booked set.
- **Fresh session on retry:** when `reconcile` has to build its own session after an earlier attempt may have posted, it calls `sync_with_books()` first. A retry then picks up where the first attempt stopped.
- **Why not sync every time:** the existing tests stub `post_line` but not `list_lines`, and I can't edit tests. A sync on the first attempt would have sent a real call to the proxy and failed them. The sync runs only after an earlier attempt got as far as booking.

The idempotency key is the existing `line.key` (`ref#n`). Retry and backoff, tool names and the books contract are unchanged. Nothing is hoisted, so this stays independent of the H1 session-hoisting change.

I edited only `reconcile.py`, though `tools.py` was in scope.
